acceptance_criteria.criterion: The function returns true only when the downstream pipeline's mostRecent.status is 'FAIL' AND it started after the upstream PASS.
The function returns false when a downstream pipeline re-engaged with PASS status after an upstream PASS.

The JSDoc comment accurately describes the refined semantics: "Returns true when a downstream agent (whose FAIL routes to Developer) has started a pipeline that resulted in FAIL since the most recent upstream PASS."
Existing tests for FAIL re-engagement scenarios continue to pass.

summary: Added `mostRecent.status === 'FAIL'` to the re-engagement detection loop in `hasDownstreamReengagedSince` — only downstream FAIL pipelines now trigger a rework signal.
Updated JSDoc to reflect refined semantics per §14.13.
Updated §14.13 row 3 test expectation from true→false: IN_PROGRESS re-engagement is no longer a rework signal (consistent with the P5 outer guard that already enforces this in production).

comments.note: §14.13 row 3 test was accurately testing the old behavior (IN_PROGRESS → true). The test required both a description update and an expectation flip to reflect the new semantics (IN_PROGRESS → false). Per WP-002 spec, P5's outer `hasDownstreamFail` guard means IN_PROGRESS never reaches this function in practice, but the unit-level contract is now correctly documented.

The `hasDownstreamReengagedSince` function is called from 3 sites (P5 in workflow-next-action.ts and two in workflow-handoff.ts), all guarded by `isMostRecentPipelineFail`. The new FAIL-only semantics at the function level makes the guard redundant but keeps the code consistent and safe for future call sites that might not carry that guard.

comments.note: AC #2 ('returns false for PASS re-engagement') has no dedicated integration test. The §14.13 test suite covers IN_PROGRESS→false (row 3) but not qa PASS→false explicitly. The condition `mostRecent.status === 'FAIL'` is unambiguous — PASS also evaluates to false — but a qa PASS test case would improve specification coverage.
Edge case verified by logic: [impl PASS, qa PASS] scenario → dsPipelines.at(-1).status = 'PASS'; condition false; returns false. Correct behavior for a successful first-run path.

Test suite update reviewed: row 3 description and expectation correctly changed from IN_PROGRESS→true to IN_PROGRESS→false. All 8 hasDownstreamReengagedSince tests pass.

Production safety confirmed: all three call sites are guarded by isMostRecentPipelineFail, so the behavioral change has zero runtime impact on existing flows. The fix improves the function's standalone contract for future call sites.

comments.note: Coverage gap (low priority, non-blocking): AC #2 ('returns false for downstream PASS re-engagement') has no dedicated test case. The IN_PROGRESS→false row 3 test covers the same code path, and the FAIL-only check is unambiguous, but an explicit test for qa PASS→false would document the contract boundary more precisely.

The refinement makes the function contract precise at the unit level even though all three call sites (P5 in workflow-next-action.ts, two in workflow-handoff.ts) are guarded by isMostRecentPipelineFail before calling this function. This is a net positive: future call sites without that outer guard will now behave correctly without silent reliance on the caller.
